problem:
Compute the following determinant using a cofactor expansion along the $3$rd row:

$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|
$$
worked_solution:
Using cofactor expansion along the third row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot {C}_{31}+2\cdot {C}_{32}+0\cdot {C}_{33}+0\cdot {C}_{34} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, computing the $3\times 3$ determinant by applying a Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot {C}_{11}+0\cdot {C}_{12}+0\cdot {C}_{13} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{1+1}\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(1\cdot 1-2\cdot (-1)) \\  & =2\cdot 3 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|=-2\cdot 6=-12.
$$
